statement: At a tax deed sale on a county-held certificate, the opening bid is the sum of all outstanding certificates on the property plus omitted years' taxes, delinquent taxes, current taxes if due, interest, and all costs and fees paid by the county. On homestead property it also includes one-half of the latest assessed value.
evidence: 2026 Florida Statutes read from the Legislature's site through a read-only capture on 2026-10-05; quoted in docs/available-amount-semantics.md section 2
office: Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller
depends_on: app.js amountInfo() / auctionBidLabel(): a Florida auction figure is the opening bid, never the final price; fees() no longer adds the homestead half

statement: A tax deed is applied for on a tax certificate: either a county-held certificate or an individual's certificate (the amount paid at application and the amount to redeem the applicant's certificate enter the opening bid). The certificate is a lien instrument held by the county or a purchaser - it is not ownership of the property, and only a tax deed application and sale can convey the land.
evidence: 2026 Florida Statutes read from the Legislature's site through a read-only capture on 2026-10-05; quoted in docs/available-amount-semantics.md section 2
office: Tax Collector (certificates); Clerk of the Circuit Court (tax deed application)
depends_on: app.js LEDGERS.certificate copy: the lien, never the land; certificate rows never show an ownership or purchase-of-land claim

statement: Property on the county's list of lands available for taxes may, after 90 days, be purchased from the clerk by anyone for the opening bid; interest on the opening bid continues to accrue through the month of sale.
